name: Community-Led Growth
summary: A go-to-market motion where an engaged community of users drives awareness, adoption, support, and retention.
explanation: Community-led growth treats the community around a product as the primary acquisition and retention channel. Members answer each other's questions, publish tutorials, build extensions, recommend the product inside their own organisations, and give the team unusually honest feedback. The motion suits products with practitioners who identify with a craft or a way of working: developer tools, creative software, knowledge management, open source. Its advantages compound: support cost per user falls as the archive of community answers grows, trust is higher because recommendations come from peers rather than from ads, and product feedback arrives continuously. Its costs are real and often underestimated. Communities need moderation, consistent presence from the company, and genuine willingness to be influenced, or they hollow out. Community-led growth also resists short-term forcing; attempts to extract leads aggressively tend to break the trust that made the community valuable. Measure it by retention, referral, and contribution rather than by direct conversion alone.

books.title: The Business of Belonging by David Spinks
